overall: Claude reviewed exact clean HEAD 1f2969c720f2ee6e023b1a77105eafa345bf5c07 and range 0444a0f..1f2969c read-only, reproduced the 62-test focused result, and found no remaining candidate-freeze blocker. The review directly exercised stale and concurrent ledger-lock behavior, close-run validation, scope-bound proof identity, uniform critique-gate reporting, operator guidance, and the version-aware tar extraction path. It confirmed that live lock holders are refused without clobbering their records, crash-stale and malformed records recover under the operating-system advisory lock, final-suite proof remains distinct from intermediate proof, and skipped critique never satisfies the mutation gate. The review reported only non-blocking portability, retention, and locking-consistency gaps plus already-disclosed residual risks.
gaps: POSIX process identity currently depends on /proc/<pid>/stat, so macOS and BSD operation is unsupported by this mechanism and is not covered by the Ubuntu and Windows CI matrix.
Ledger lock tombstones and run records have no bounded cleanup path and therefore accumulate with the number of runs.
InvocationStore terminal and expiry transitions remain unlocked read-modify-write operations even though the run ledger now uses per-record advisory locking.
risks: The fully_trusted tar extraction filter intentionally makes the explicit prevalidation loop the sole archive-member barrier; future archive-format changes must preserve that validation.
A failed tombstone write can conservatively refuse a contender for up to the sixty-second lease window before recovery.
Pre-mutation critique is a gate input rather than an interlock; the process runner or pilot must enforce refusal when gate_satisfied is false.
High-impact classification remains caller-declared judgment through objective_properties.
Evidence and proof stores remain unsigned and user-writable, and default phase and run envelopes remain uncalibrated.
